title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — if 'death' = all penalties, hereditary vice still not among them
pass_a_gloss: You take that entering sin as Adam's bare act, and its wage as chiefly spiritual death—privation of original righteousness plus hereditary corruption—so that corruption sits under the word death here. I have already shown it does not. If Paul by death meant every penalty derived from Adam, yet still did not fold hereditary vice into that name, then hereditary vice is not among the penalties Adam brought on the world, and his act was not imputed unto that penalty.
pass_b_english: But you will have that sin to be Adam's actual sin, and its penalty to be not only the death of the body and eternal death, but chiefly the spiritual death of the soul, placed in the privation of original righteousness, and in hereditary corruption: from which it follows that that corruption is contained under the name of death in this place. And yet I have already proved that it is not contained. But if the Apostle by the name of death signified whatever of penalty was derived through Adam into his posterity, and yet did not under that name embrace hereditary corruption or vice, as I have already proved, you see what follows, namely that that hereditary vice is not in the number of the penalties which Adam brought upon the world, and therefore that his actual sin was not imputed to the world unto that penalty, namely hereditary vice.
source_text: Tu autem vis illud peccatum esse peccatum actuale Adami, & illius poenam esse non tantum mortem corporis & aeternam, sed imprimis mortem spiritualem animae, positam in privatione iustitiae originalis, & corruptione haereditaria: Ex quo sequitur istam corruptionem nomine mortis hoc loco contineri. Atqui iam probavi non contineri. Quod si Apostolus mortis nomine quicquid poenae per Adamum in posteros derivatum est significavit, nec tamen eo nomine corruptionem haereditariam seu vitium complexus est, ut iam probavi, vides quid sequatur, nempe vitium illud haereditarium non esse in numero poenarum quas Adamus mundo intulit, ac proinde peccatum eius actuale non esse mundo imputatum ad illam poenam, videlicet vitium haereditarium.

choices.choice: Even if death = all penalties, hereditary vice still not among them—so actual not imputed unto that penalty
